newsitem.title: UK: Australia tops bond markets in latest week - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Australia tops bond markets in latest week - Salomon.

text.p: Australian bond markets were the best performers in the latest week, according to data from Salomon Brothers on Friday.
Australian bonds, helped by a benign inflation report in the past week and expectations of subdued earnings data, showed a 0.98 percent gain in the week ended April 16 in local currency terms.
They were well ahead of the next top two markets, Ireland and Britain, which showed 0.59 percent and 0.52 percent returns in their respective local currencies.
Overall, the 17-country bond index rose 0.18 percent. Only three markets showed losses in the week, each of them narrow, with Japan losing 0.07 percent, Sweden 0.04 percent and Finland 0.02 percent.
U.S. Treasuries eeked out a modest gain, returning 0.09 percent.

In U.S. dollar terms, all but six markets made losses. The worst performer was Finland which lost dollar-based investors 0.97 percent. Switzerland was the top gainer, returning 0.68 percent in dollars.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
